review_comments.body: **Visibility tracking starts too late** If a background tab becomes visible while the tracker waits for `readystatechange`, `initPerformance()` reads the page as visible and sets `firstHiddenTime` to `Infinity`. The buffered FCP/LCP entries then pass the cutoff, including the long wait before the tab became visible. Those inflated values still skew p75. Capture visibility and attach the listener when the tracker script starts, before waiting to initialize the collector.

**Paint cutoff tests miss paths** `FakeObserver` delivers every supplied entry before the page changes visibility. The tests also supply no paint entries through `getEntriesByType`. Both tests would still pass if the new fallback filters or the listener that saves the hide time were removed. Add cases with fallback entries and delayed observer delivery across a visible-to-hidden transition. That would protect these separate parts of the fix from regressions. Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!

**[Medium impact]** The change reaches FCP and LCP metrics from tracked pages\. The PR needs an earlier visibility snapshot before merging so background-loaded pages cannot bypass the new cutoff.

Findings

Summary

The PR filters FCP and LCP against the first recorded hide time and adds tests for initially hidden and visible pages. - Performance reports skip paints after a page first becomes hidden.
